items.title: Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1): corner charts and corner structures

book.label: §4.1, Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147)
book.statement: An M-polyfold $X$ has a compatible smooth manifold structure with boundary with corners if it admits an atlas of sc-smoothly compatible charts $(V, \varphi, (U, C, \mathbb R^n))$, $\varphi : V \to U$ an sc-diffeomorphism from an open $V \subseteq X$ onto a relatively open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$ in $\mathbb R^n$ (or in a finite-dimensional vector space).

lean.statement: A corner chart (`MChart.IsCornerChart`) is a chart whose model is $(U, C, V)$ with $V$ finite-dimensional, the constant sc-structure, $U$ relatively open in the partial quadrant $C$, and the identity retraction. `HasCornerStructure`: an atlas of corner charts equivalent to the atlas of $X$; equivalently every point lies in a corner chart that is a chart of $X$. The dimension may vary. Corner models are tame retracts and sc⁺-retracts; a corner structure makes $X$ tame.

diff: "Sc-smoothly compatible" and "$\varphi$ an sc-diffeomorphism" are read as compatibility with the atlas of $X$, as for tameness (Findings, Chapter 4, item 50).
The classical manifold structure is represented by the corner atlas; local constancy of the dimension is neither stated nor formalized.

(2026-11-09) With the dimension fixed (`HasCornerStructureOfDim P n`), a corner structure gives a Mathlib `ChartedSpace (EuclideanQuadrant n)` with `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant n) ∞`, and `IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞` without boundary (`cornerChartedSpace`, `isManifold_cornerChartedSpace`, `isManifold_interiorChartedSpace`); the partial quadrants of the charts are translated into the full quadrant, since a Mathlib manifold has one model (`Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge.lean`; gap G.102).

book.statement: A finite-dimensional Banach space $E$ has precisely one sc-structure, namely the constant structure $E_m = E$.

items.title: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): $1_1^0$, $1_0^1$, and the constant structure

book.label: §4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)
book.statement: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ has the inverse $1_1^0$, which is always sc-smooth; so if $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth it is an sc-diffeomorphism. It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the underlying sets agree. A finite-dimensional space with the constant structure has $X = X^1$.

lean.statement: $1_1^0 : X^1 \to X$ is sc-smooth (in charts the sc-operator $\iota : E^1 \to E$). If $X = X_1$ as sets and $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth, it is an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $1_1^0$. For a finite-dimensional $V$: $(\mathrm{const}\,V)^1 = \mathrm{const}\,V$, the lift is the identity, every retract is an sc⁺-retract. **The example** (`remark_4_1_3_example`): an M-polyfold with $X_0 = X_\infty$ for which $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is not sc-smooth, so $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds; it is a retract $O = O_\infty \subseteq \mathbb R \oplus X$ that is not an sc⁺-retract (`remark_4_1_3_retract_example`), the image of the retraction $(t, z) \mapsto (t, L(t)z)$ of moving rank-one projections on a weighted sequence space, sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss (`IsLossFamily.isScSmooth`). $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (`MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff`).

diff: “It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the sets agree” is proved by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give (fourth addendum of this page; formerly gap G.31); the 2021 edition (p. 176) gives a different one, the space of its Subsection 1.4.4, which is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). By Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8) an example is a retract $O = O_\infty$ that is not an sc⁺-retract; it cannot come from a retraction whose level maps are $C^1$ (an argument, not formalized), so its retraction loses a level in its first derivative, as the splicings of HWZ do, and its sc-smoothness rests on a criterion with loss proved for it, not on Proposition 1.2.4 (preprint 1.19). In the example $X$ and $X^1$ even have different topologies on the same set (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

“$X^1 \ne X$” is read as “$1_0^1$ is not sc-smooth”, equivalently (by `remark_4_1_3_isScDiffeo`) “the identity is not an sc-diffeomorphism $X \to X^1$”. The sc-diffeomorphism clause needs only $X = X_1$, not $X_0 = X_\infty$. “$(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$” misprints $X_0$; $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ holds as sets and with the topologies of the iterated levels (`MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, V2.93; gap G.6, closed) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 5, 125). Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the missing example).

lean.statement: `lemma_4_5_1`: for an sc-smooth $f : X \to Y$ of M-polyfolds and sc-smooth vector fields $A$, $B$ on $X$, $A'$, $B'$ on $Y$ with $Tf(A(x)) = A'(f_1(x))$ and $Tf(B(x)) = B'(f_1(x))$ for all $x \in X^1$ (`liftLevelOneMap`), $Tf([A, B](x)) = [A', B'](f_2(x))$ for all $x \in X^2$ (`levelTwoMap`).

diff: More general in the map: any sc-smooth $f$ between two M-polyfolds, with a pair of vector fields on each side. The relations are assumed on all of $X^1$, not only at the points of $X_2$, since the computation of §4.5.2 differentiates them. A local sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of $X$ is covered only through such an $f$; open subsets of an M-polyfold as M-polyfolds are not built (gap G.92) (Findings, Chapter 4, item 162).

items.title: Lemma 4.4.4 on an M-polyfold, $i = 1$: $A^{(1)} = \Phi^{-1} \circ A_1$

book.label: §4.4, Lemma 4.4.4, p. 196
book.statement: (New in the 2021 edition.) By the natural identification of $(TX)^i \to (X^1)^i$ with $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$, the index of a vector field $A$ can be raised by $i \ge 0$: $A^{(i)}$ is an sc-smooth vector field of $X^i$, a section of $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$.

lean.statement: For every $i$, $A^{(i)}$ ($A^{(0)} = A$, $A^{(i+1)} = (A^{(i)})^{(1)}$) is an sc-smooth vector field on $X^i$, whose image under $T(X^i) \to TX$ at $x \in X^{i+1}$ is $A(x)$, and $\Phi_i \circ A^{(i)} \circ J_i$ is the $i$-th index raise of $A$ (`lemma_4_4_4_all`, V4.79). The case first recorded here: `raiseIndex hA` $= \Phi^{-1} \circ A_1 : X^2 \to T(X^1)$, with $\Phi : T(X^1) \simeq (TX)^1$ of Proposition 2.3.17; `lemma_4_4_4`: $A^{(1)}$ is an sc-smooth vector field on $X^1$, and $\Phi(A^{(1)}(x)) = A(x)$ in $(TX)^1$.

diff: Proved in full in V4.79; the narrower form first recorded here is kept (`lemma_4_4_4`, $i = 1$).

For $i = 1$; every $i$ is V4.79, by iterating this case. The identification that the text calls natural is Proposition 2.3.17 (`proposition_2_3_17`, `proposition_2_3_17_two`, and for every $i$ `proposition_2_3_17_all`; gap G.6, closed) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 160, 164).

items.title: Lemma 4.4.4 on an M-polyfold, every $i$: $A^{(i)}$

book.label: §4.4, Lemma 4.4.4, p. 196
book.statement: (New in the 2021 edition.) By the natural identification of $(TX)^i \to (X^1)^i$ with $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$, the index of a vector field $A$ can be raised by $i \ge 0$: $A^{(i)}$ is an sc-smooth vector field of $X^i$, a section of $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$ (the diagram before the lemma).

lean.statement: `BundledMPolyfold.raiseIndexAll`: $A^{(0)} = A$, $A^{(i+1)} = (A^{(i)})^{(1)}$ (`raiseIndex` on $X^i$). `lemma_4_4_4_all`: for every $i$, $A^{(i)}$ is an sc-smooth vector field on $X^i$ (`BundledMPolyfold.lift`); its image under $T(X^i) \to TX$ at $x \in X^{i+1}$ is $A(x)$ (`tangentIncl_raiseIndexAll`); $\Phi_i \circ A^{(i)} \circ J_i$ is the $i$-th index raise of $A$ (`tangentLiftEquiv_raiseIndexAll`, with $\Phi_i$, $J_i$ of `proposition_2_3_17_all`); and $A^{(i+1)} = (A^{(i)})^{(1)}$. Witness: `lemma_4_4_4_all_zero`.

diff: The lifts $X^i$ are bundled with their spaces so that they form one family indexed by $i$. "The natural identification" is $\Phi_i : T(X^i) \to (TX)^i$ and $J_i : (X^1)^i \to (X^i)^1$ of Proposition 2.3.17 for every $i$; "$A^{(i)}$ is $A$" is read through the inclusions into $TX$ and through the diagram printed before the lemma (Findings, Chapter 4, item 164).

notFormalized.title: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): “$X^1 \ne X$ is possible”
notFormalized.label: §4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)
notFormalized.book: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, then $X_m = X_0$ as sets for all $m$; "however, it is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as sc-smooth spaces despite the fact that $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$ as sets".
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (fourth addendum; V4.6), by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give. The 2021 edition (p. 176) adds an example: the space of its Subsection 1.4.4 (a line with a half-plane attached), made an M-polyfold with $X_\infty = X$, for which $1_0^1$ cannot be sc-smooth, since Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) would make $X$ a manifold of constant local dimension; that argument holds as we read it and is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). On the weighted sequence space $X$ of V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k(k+1)^m|x_k|$), $L(t)$ is the projection onto $\cos\theta\,e_{n_k} + \sin\theta\,e_{n_{k+1}}$ ($n_k = 2^k$), the angle $\theta$ turning from $0$ to $\pi/2$ with flat ends while $t$ runs through $[1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)]$, and $L(t) = 0$ for $t \le 0$. The retraction $r(t, z) = (t, L(t)z)$ of $\mathbb R \oplus X$ is sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss; its retract $O$ consists of smooth points, and the lift $O \to E_1$ is discontinuous at $0$, so $O$ is not an sc⁺-retract (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8)), and the M-polyfold $O$ with its single chart has $X_0 = X_\infty$ and $1_0^1$ not sc-smooth. Why an example needs a retraction that loses a level (one with $C^1$ level maps gives none) is an argument, not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10): the section $u \mapsto (1 - p)(u - t(u))$ is sc-Fredholm
notFormalized.label: §4.1, Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10), pp. 179–181 (preprint pp. 151–153)
notFormalized.book: The section $u \mapsto (u, \mathbf f(u))$, $\mathbf f(u) = (1 - p)(u - t(u))$, of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ is sc-Fredholm.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized, because no longer used**: Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9), its only use, is proved directly (V4.20–V4.25). It would need $U \triangleleft Y$ as a strong bundle, $Y$ and $Y \cap F$ as sc-subspaces, the sc-isomorphism $E \cong (T_0O \oplus B) \oplus W$ with $B \subseteq Y_\infty$, and at each smooth point the re-centred strong bundle chart (V4.18), filler and conjugation. The text's proof has a sign slip in $D\mathbf f(u)$, calls $D\mathbf f(u)$ an sc⁺-operator, writes $L(T_0O)$ for $L(Y)$, and omits the interior points of $(T_0O \oplus B) \cap C$ (Findings, item 57).

notFormalized.title: Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14): the local form near $\{d_X = 0\}$
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14), p. 184 (preprint p. 157)
notFormalized.book: Near points $a \in A$ with $d_X(a) = 0$ the submanifold $A$ is a smooth finite-dimensional manifold in the classical sense.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized in part since the first edition of this page** (V4.32). Near the points with $d_X(a) = 0$, the preprint's wording, $A$ is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold with a corner structure on an open neighbourhood, without tameness of $X$ (`remark_4_2_2_interior`, `remark_4_2_2_near`); globally if $d_X = 0$ on all of $A$ (`hasCornerStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero`). **Not formalized**: the 2021 wording, near the points $a \in A$ with $d_A(a) = 0$ (more points, since $d_A \le d_X$), and the 2021 sentence that near $d_A(a) = 1$ the set $A$ is a smooth manifold with boundary (Findings, Chapter 4, items 61, 165).

notFormalized.title: The open question after Proposition 4.2.3 (preprint 4.15)
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Open Question, preprint p. 159
notFormalized.book: Is a sub-M-polyfold with $A = A_\infty$ and $\dim T_aA$ finite and locally constant a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold? Is the "T" $\{(x, 0) : |x| < 1\} \cup \{(0, y) : 0 \le y < 1\}$ homeomorphic to a retract $O = O_\infty$? Impossible for sc⁺-retracts.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (a question, not a statement). The last sentence, for a retract without boundary, is V4.32 with $A = O$: an sc⁺-retract in $(O, E, E)$ is a manifold; that the "T" is not a topological manifold is not formalized (Findings, item 65).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.2.11 (1) (preprint 4.22): local faces of the chart as global local faces
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Theorem 4.2.11 (1) (preprint 4.22), p. 190 (preprint p. 162)
notFormalized.book: There are precisely $d = d_X(x)$ local faces $F_1, \dots, F_d$ contained in $U$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized for the chart model only** (V4.50): $d_X(x) = n$, all coordinates vanish at the centre, and $\psi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$. The identification of these faces with (germs of) global faces of $X$ (Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45) in the face-structured case) is not formalized (Findings, items 86, 90). The text's local faces are faces of the neighbourhood $U$ itself (closures in $U$ of the components of $U \cap \{d_X = 1\}$), so (4) is affected as well; the missing step is a local face theorem for small neighbourhoods, believed true for tame $X$ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 130; third addendum).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23): chart independence of stratified regularity
notFormalized.label: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166)
notFormalized.book: Regular values of the maps $p_\sigma : A \cap F_\sigma^\circ \to \mathbb R^m$, intrinsic to $A$ and its strata.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** Stratified regularity is defined in some product chart (V4.53); its independence of the chart is true by the transport argument of V4.39 (the transition maps of product charts are $\mathrm{id} \times \tau$ up to translation) but not formalized. Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) is unaffected: it produces $\Sigma$ (Findings, items 102, 108).

notFormalized.title: Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25): sc-differential forms and the directed system
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25), p. 195 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: An sc-differential $k$-form is an sc-smooth $\omega : \oplus^kTX \to \mathbb R$, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric; pull-back along $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ gives a directed system with limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs $\oplus^kTX$ as an M-polyfold, a linear $T_xX$ (gap G.7) and the M-polyfolds $X^i$ for $i \ge 2$ with $(TX)^i \cong T(X^i)$ (gap G.6, closed by Proposition 2.3.17 for every $i$). The text writes $\Omega^*_\infty$ for both the limit and the sum (Findings, item 124). (2026-11-09) The linear structure of $T_xX$ is now formalized (gap G.7 closed, V2.19); the other ingredients remain.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26): the Lie bracket of sc-smooth vector fields
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: (2021) For sc-smooth vector fields $A$, $B$ on $X$ the usual formula defines an sc-smooth section $[A, B]$ of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$, proved in Appendix 4.5 (§§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202). The preprint and 2017 texts state an sc-smooth vector field on $X^1$, a section of $T(X^1) \to X^2$, quoted from another paper.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V4.74–V4.77), on an M-polyfold: $[A, B] : X^2 \to TX$, the bracket of the principal parts in any chart, is sc-smooth and covers the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$ (`proposition_4_4_5`, V4.76), independently of the chart (V4.75), by Lemma 4.5.1, whose proof the text leaves to the reader and which is proved by the computation of §4.5.2 in a local model (V4.74) and on M-polyfolds for every sc-smooth map (V4.77); the local model is V4.67–V4.72 (gap G.38, closed). "Section of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$" is read as a map $X^2 \to TX$ over the inclusion; the pull-back bundle itself and Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets are gap G.92. The sentence of p. 201 that the bracket at $x \in O_2$ lies on level $1$ does not hold as we read it (V4.73) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 155–157, 161, 162).

notFormalized.title: The exterior derivative, Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27) and the relative complex
notFormalized.label: §4.4, pp. 195–199 (preprint pp. 167–168), Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27)
notFormalized.book: $d : \Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^i)$ by the usual formula, $d^2 = 0$; $H^*_{sc}(X) = \ker d/\operatorname{im} d$; the relative complex $\Omega^*_\infty(X) \oplus \Omega^{*-1}_\infty(\partial X)$ with $d(\omega, \tau) = (d\omega, j^*\omega - d\tau)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The direction of $d$ should presumably be $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ (the bracket lives one level up); $d \circ d = 0$ and $dj^* = j^*d$ are asserted without proof; forms on $\partial X$, a union of faces, are not defined (Findings, items 120–122).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28): Stokes' theorem
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28), p. 199 (preprint p. 168)
notFormalized.book: For an oriented compact tame smooth $n$-dimensional submanifold $N$ whose boundary is a union of faces $F$, and an sc-differential $(n - 1)$-form $\omega$, $\int_N d\omega = \sum_F\int_F\omega$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (no proof in the text; integration on manifolds with corners of varying dimension is not in Mathlib). The formula writes $\int_M$ for $\int_N$ (Findings, item 123).

notFormalized.title: 2021 §4.4 and Appendix 4.5: sc-differential forms, the exterior derivative, Stokes, the Poincaré lemma
notFormalized.label: §4.4 and Appendix 4.5, pp. 195–208 (2021)
notFormalized.book: Definitions 4.4.1–4.4.2 (forms on the Whitney sum $\oplus_kTX$, the direct limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$), the exterior derivative $d : \Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ with $d^2 = 0$, Definition 4.4.6 and the relative complex, Theorem 4.4.7 (Stokes), the Poincaré Lemma 4.4.8 (p. 199) and its local form Lemma 4.5.2 (p. 202, proved in §4.5.3).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (continues G.37–G.40). It needs $\oplus_kTX$ as an M-polyfold bundle, a linear $T_xX$ (gap G.7), the M-polyfolds $X^i$ with $(TX)^i \cong T(X^i)$ for all $i$ (gap G.6, closed), and integration on manifolds with corners. The vector fields of Definition 4.4.3, Lemma 4.4.4 (for every $i$), the bracket of Proposition 4.4.5 and Lemma 4.5.1 are formalized, in a local model (V4.67–V4.72, V4.74) and on an M-polyfold (V4.68, V4.75–V4.79). The 2021 text runs $d$ as G.39 proposed and writes $\int_N$; in the displayed formula for $d\omega$ (p. 197) the sign $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ and the summation index $i$ are possible misprints for $(-1)^{\ell+j}$ and $j$ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 158). (2026-11-09) The linear structure of $T_xX$ is now formalized (gap G.7 closed, V2.19); the other ingredients remain.

notFormalized.title: Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets; the pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5, p. 196, and Appendix 4.5, Lemma 4.5.1, p. 201 (2021)
notFormalized.book: (New in the 2021 edition.) Lemma 4.5.1: a local sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi : X \to X$ that relates two vector fields relates their brackets. Proposition 4.4.5: the bracket is an sc-smooth section of the pull-back $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ of $TX \to X^1$ by the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized for every sc-smooth map $f : X \to Y$ of M-polyfolds** (V4.77), with the relations on $X^1$, and with the bracket an sc-smooth map $X^2 \to TX$ over the inclusion (V4.76). **Not formalized:** a local sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of $X$, which would need open subsets of an M-polyfold as M-polyfolds (it is covered only when it is the restriction of such an $f$), and the pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ as a bundle object (Findings, Chapter 4, item 163).
